* **Description of issue**

Tim13 is a chaperone of the intermembrane space. It does associate with proteins at both the OMM (TOM complex) and the IMM (TIM22 or 23 , i forget) , but it isn't a membrane protein

Essential for the function of the TIM22 pathway (they guide precursors from TOM to TIM22).

Sometimes transiently associated with TIM22 during substrate handoff.

Occasionally found in co-purification experiments under certain conditions.

❌ But they are not:
Integral membrane components of the TIM22 complex.

Stably bound subunits included in structural definitions of the complex.

Encoded in structural proteomics maps of the TIM22 complex proper.

author: ValWood
body: I think its the same. The human names are misleading though. TIMM13 has the name translocase of inner mitochondrial membrane 13 but these proteins are chaperones that act as a ratchet to ensure the proteins move forward through the translocase, and then assist them across the IMM. There are 2 TIM associated complexes: Called Tim8-Tim13 complex Tim9-Tim10 complex in yeast if it's really tricky the IMM annotation is probably OK, they do associated with the IMM, but it isn't ideal... https://www.mdpi.com/2218-273X/10/7/1008
